meta.title: DHAKA METRO INTELLIGENCE
meta.project: Dhaka Mass Rapid Transit Development Project - MRT Line-6
meta.dataset: Packaged dataset (MRT Line-6 analytical package, Phases 1-4)
meta.geoNote: Track geometry and station stop positions from OpenStreetMap relation 15060935 (Dhaka Metro Rail Line 6), 241 vertices, 18.97 km between Uttara North and Motijheel stop positions. (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL.
meta.disclaimer: Operational figures are SYNTHETIC simulations calibrated to published totals. They are not a DMTCL feed.
meta.contextNote: Station descriptions and nearby places are descriptive context written for this dashboard, not a dataset. Catchment population is not available from public sources.

stations.name: Uttara North
stations.summary: Northern terminus beside the Diabari depot; RAJUK Uttara third-phase housing still filling in.
stations.commercial: Uttara Sector 18 apartment project; Diabari lakeside
stations.education: Private universities' permanent campuses in Uttara third phase
stations.transport: Local buses and human haulers to Uttara and Mirpur; rickshaws

stations.name: Uttara Center
stations.summary: Planned as the centre of the Uttara third-phase township; RAJUK land earmarked for transit-oriented development nearby.

stations.name: Uttara South
stations.summary: Lowest-demand station on the line; surrounded by partly built residential plots.

stations.name: Pallabi
stations.summary: Dense residential Mirpur; serves Mirpur 12, Mirpur DOHS and the cantonment edge.
stations.transport: City buses on Begum Rokeya Avenue; human haulers; rickshaws

stations.name: Mirpur 11
stations.summary: Mixed residential and neighbourhood retail along Begum Rokeya Avenue.
stations.commercial: Mirpur 11 kitchen market; Purobi area shops

stations.name: Mirpur 10
stations.summary: Mirpur's main junction and one of the busiest stations; damaged in July 2024 and reopened 15 October 2024.
stations.transport: Major bus interchange (Mirpur 1, 2, 13, 14); Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium nearby

stations.name: Kazipara
stations.summary: Residential corridor station; closed after the July 2024 unrest and reopened 20 September 2024.
stations.commercial: Furniture and household shops on Begum Rokeya Avenue

stations.name: Agargaon
stations.summary: Government office district; terminus of the first section opened in December 2022.
stations.commercial: IDB Bhaban computer market; office district
stations.health: National Institute of Neurosciences; Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital; other national institutes
stations.transport: Buses on Mirpur Road and Rokeya Avenue; passport and election commission offices nearby

stations.name: Bijoy Sarani
stations.summary: Between the parliament complex and the old Tejgaon airport; one of the quieter stations.
stations.transport: Buses on Bijoy Sarani; Novo Theatre and military museum nearby

stations.name: Farmgate
stations.summary: One of Dhaka's busiest road interchanges, with coaching centres, colleges and offices.
stations.commercial: Farmgate markets; Green Road and Indira Road commerce
stations.education: Tejgaon College; Government Science College; Holy Cross College
stations.health: Hospitals and clinics on Green Road
stations.transport: Major bus interchange; Dhaka Elevated Expressway ramp; Khamarbari

stations.name: Karwan Bazar
stations.summary: Wholesale market and corporate office district with media houses and hotels.
stations.commercial: Karwan Bazar wholesale market; corporate towers; Bashundhara City mall at Panthapath
stations.transport: Buses on Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue; Tejgaon railway station about 1 km

stations.name: Shahbagh
stations.summary: Hospital and cultural district at the edge of the university area.
stations.education: Dhaka University (north side); Faculty of Fine Arts
stations.health: Bangladesh Medical University (formerly BSMMU); BIRDEM General Hospital
stations.transport: Buses at Shahbagh intersection; National Museum and Public Library nearby

stations.name: Dhaka University
stations.summary: Serves the main university campus; demand follows the academic calendar and the February book fair.
stations.education: University of Dhaka; BUET within about 1 km
stations.health: Dhaka Medical College Hospital about 1 km
stations.transport: Rickshaws; campus buses; Suhrawardy Udyan and Bangla Academy adjacent

stations.name: Bangladesh Secretariat
stations.transport: Buses at Paltan and Press Club; Supreme Court nearby

stations.name: Motijheel
stations.summary: Dhaka's traditional financial centre and the busiest station; southern terminus until the Kamalapur extension opens.
stations.commercial: Bank and corporate headquarters; Bangladesh Bank
stations.transport: City buses; Kamalapur railway station about 1 km (extension under construction)

milestones.text: Project implementation period begins
Original DPP approved by ECNEC (Tk 21,985.07 crore; completion June 2024)
JICA loan agreement (I) signed - 10,477 mn yen
JICA loan agreement (II) signed - 75,571 mn yen
1st revision (no cost change)
JICA loan agreement (III) signed - 79,271 mn yen
JICA loan agreement (IV) signed - 72,194 mn yen
JICA loan agreement (V) signed - 18,285 mn yen
2nd revision approved by ECNEC (Tk 33,471.99 crore; to Dec 2025; adds Kamalapur extension)
Inauguration of Uttara North-Agargaon section (11.73 km)
Commercial service begins (Uttara North and Agargaon stations only)
All nine stations of first section open
Inauguration of Agargaon-Motijheel section
Commercial service to Motijheel (Farmgate, Secretariat, Motijheel stations)
All 16 stations in passenger service
Service suspended amid unrest; Mirpur-10 and Kazipara stations vandalised on 19 July
Service resumed excluding Mirpur-10 and Kazipara
Kazipara station reopened
Mirpur-10 station reopened
Bearing pad fell at Farmgate section killing a pedestrian; service briefly suspended
Planning Commission PEC clears 3rd revision
3rd revision approved by ECNEC (Tk 32,717.73 crore; to Dec 2028)
